bio: My research focuses on developing scalable, causally-informed machine learning methods for large-scale, heterogeneous multivariate time series, where data are high-dimensional, noisy, sparse, and subject to regime shift. My work begins with a deep understanding of the data, such as its structure, causal dependencies, and sources of shift and sparsity, uses that understanding to develop efficient and robust learning algorithms, and validates them on real-world data from high-impact complex dynamic systems. Over 12 years of data-centric research and practice, I have worked at the intersection of computing and application domains, collaborating closely with experts in industry and enterprise systems, public health, and sustainability to bridge domain knowledge and data-driven modeling, and to turn large, messy real-world data into reliable forecasts and actionable decisions.

futureLab.heading: Causal intelligence for complex dynamic systems
futureLab.text: I will establish a research lab at the intersection of AI, data systems, and causality, focused on forecasting when data are sparse and dynamics are changing. The five-year agenda covers causal discovery under sparsity with LLM-based agents, time series foundation models pretrained on simulation ensembles, and open systems and benchmarks for causally-constrained streaming forecasting, with applications in public health, sustainability, and critical infrastructure. I am on the 2026–27 academic job market and welcome conversations with search committees and prospective collaborators.
